highlightAliases.old: Azithromycin 250 mg daily or 3×/week reduces exacerbations in former smokers; watch for QTc, hearing loss, resistance (p1254).
highlightAliases.new: Azithromycin 250 mg daily or 3×/week reduces exacerbations in former smokers; watch for QTc, hearing loss, resistance; maintenance may be considered for frequent exacerbators despite maximal triple inhalers when worsening airflow obstruction and airway inflammation drive symptoms, without hearing impairment, resting tachycardia or other arrhythmia, apparent QTc-prolongation risk, or clinical/radiographic NTM evidence, with NTM assessment before regular use (p1254).

highlightAliases.old: COPD is currently the 4th leading cause of death in the US; projected to be the 5th leading cause of disability and 3rd cause of death worldwide by 2030 (p1235).
highlightAliases.new: Hazzard cited an earlier US mortality ranking and projected COPD to rank fifth for disability and third for death worldwide by 2030 (p1235). In CDC's final 2024 US statistics, the broader category chronic lower respiratory diseases, which includes COPD and asthma, ranked fifth.

highlightAliases.old: Half of adults with COPD will be ≥75 years old by 2030 (p1235).
highlightAliases.new: The chapter projected that people aged 75 or older would account for about half of adults with COPD by 2030 (p1235).

highlightAliases.old: GOLD criterion: fixed FEV1/FVC < 0.70 — doesn't correct for age, overdiagnoses older adults (prevalence 37.7% by GOLD vs 15.4% by age-adjusted Z-score) (p1243–1244).
highlightAliases.new: In a compatible clinical context, GOLD uses post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC <0.70. Because the fixed ratio does not adjust for age, it can classify more older adults as obstructed than an age-adjusted lower limit of normal. In the older cohort described here, estimates were 37.7% versus 15.4% (p1244, Table 81-5).

highlightAliases.old: ATS/ERS FEV1 staging thresholds: ≥70% Pred = mild, 50–69% = moderate, <50% = severe (p1244, Table 81-5).
highlightAliases.new: Table 81-5 reproduces older ATS/ERS categories using FEV1 percent predicted: ≥70%, 50–69% and <50% (p1244). The 2022 ERS/ATS interpretive standard grades impairment by z-score. GOLD's airflow-obstruction grades are a separate framework.

highlightAliases.old: PRISm = preserved FEV1/FVC ratio but low FEV1 + inflammatory-airway features — still at risk (p1244).
highlightAliases.new: PRISm is a post-bronchodilator spirometric pattern with FEV1/FVC ≥0.70 and FEV1 <80% predicted. It can be associated with respiratory symptoms or later airflow obstruction. Demonstrating airway inflammation is not part of its definition (p1244, GOLD).

highlightAliases.old: Stepwise approach: SABA rescue → long-acting BD (LAMA usually first-line, greater exacerbation reduction than LABA) → add the other class → add ICS (combined with a LABA — ICS monotherapy is not recommended in COPD, unlike asthma) for frequent exacerbations not controlled by LABA and/or LAMA, hospitalization for exacerbation, or concomitant asthma; ICS+LABA reduces exacerbations/hospitalizations with eosinophils ≥300 cells/mL [sic — the book's own Table 81-7, p1246, gives cells/μL] plus high symptom burden and frequent exacerbations (p1253; agents in Table 81-10, p1249–1252).
highlightAliases.new: COPD inhaled treatment: offer a short-acting rescue bronchodilator. GOLD 2026 generally favors LABA/LAMA for symptomatic group B or exacerbation-prone group E patients and considers LABA/LAMA/ICS in group E at eosinophils ≥300 cells/μL. Following exacerbations on LABA/LAMA, ICS benefit is more likely as the eosinophil count rises. Concomitant asthma requires an ICS-containing regimen. Table 81-7 gives cells/μL; the p1253 prose prints cells/mL (Table 81-10, p1249–1252; GOLD treatment algorithms).

highlightAliases.old: ICS risks in older adults: 1.2–1.6-fold increased pneumonia risk (highest with older age, frailty, low BMI, high dose, eosinophils <100 cells/mL [sic — the book's own Table 81-7, p1246, gives cells/μL]); ↓ bone mineral density above 1000 mcg/day fluticasone-equivalent; posterior subcapsular cataracts; atypical mycobacterial infection (p1253–1254).
highlightAliases.new: ICS risks in older adults: 1.2–1.6-fold increased pneumonia risk (highest with older age, frailty, low BMI, high dose, eosinophils <100 cells/μL); ↓ bone mineral density above 1000 mcg/day fluticasone-equivalent; subcapsular cataracts are established with systemic steroids, while causation with ICS is less certain; atypical mycobacterial infection (p1253–1254).

highlightAliases.old: Lung transplant referral thresholds: FEV1/DLCO <25% predicted, PaCO2 >50 mmHg, BODE >5; median post-transplant survival 5–6 years; age >70 has higher 30-day/1-year mortality (p1258–1259).
highlightAliases.new: Lung transplant referral thresholds: both FEV1 and DLCO <25% predicted, PaCO2 >50 mmHg, BODE >5; median post-transplant survival 5–6 years; age >70 has higher 30-day/1-year mortality (p1258–1259).

highlightAliases.old: ICS combined with LABA reduces exacerbations and hospitalizations with absolute eosinophil count ≥300 cells/mL plus high symptom burden and frequent exacerbations (GOLD Group D).
highlightAliases.new: ICS combined with LABA reduces exacerbations and hospitalizations with absolute eosinophil count ≥300 cells/μL plus high symptom burden and frequent exacerbations (GOLD Group D).

highlightAliases.old: Pneumonia risk with ICS is greatest with eosinophils <100 cells/mL (also older age, frailty, low BMI, high ICS dose); ICS withdrawal can be considered with eosinophils <300 (especially <100) cells/mL (p1253–1254). [sic — the book's own Table 81-7, p1246, gives cells/μL]
highlightAliases.new: Pneumonia risk with ICS is greatest with eosinophils <100 cells/μL (also older age, frailty, low BMI, high ICS dose); ICS withdrawal can be considered with eosinophils <300 (especially <100) cells/μL (p1253–1254). (Table 81-7, p1246, and GOLD Figure 3.10 use cells/μL; the prose on p1253 prints cells/mL.)

highlightAliases.old: LVRS candidates: FEV1 <50% predicted, RV >150–200% predicted, upper-lobe-predominant emphysema; FEV1 or DLCO <20% predicted + homogeneous emphysema = higher surgical mortality, do not operate (p1258).
highlightAliases.new: LVRS candidates: FEV1 <50% predicted, RV >150–200% predicted, upper-lobe-predominant emphysema; For surgical risk, check the original NETT definition: FEV₁ at most 20% predicted, together with either homogeneous emphysema on CT or DLCO at most 20% predicted. This subgroup had excess operative mortality and little functional benefit. Page 1258 groups the criteria differently. NETT high-risk analysis.

highlightAliases.old: FEV1 or DLCO < 20% predicted with homogeneous (rather than upper-lobe-predominant) emphysema — higher surgical mortality; should not undergo LVRS (p1258).
highlightAliases.new: In NETT, FEV₁ at most 20% predicted plus either homogeneous emphysema or DLCO at most 20% predicted identified patients at high surgical risk. The 30-day mortality was 16% after surgery versus 0% with medical treatment. Page 1258 phrases the criteria differently. Original NETT analysis.
